analysis.title: GS McGeoch - Copper Oversold? ...Insurance premiums and Anglo cadence
key_insights: The author argues copper at $12.5k, down from $14.5k, has had a lot of risk premium removed, and frames a small long position as an insurance-premium trade.
The morning note flagged CTAs short, China speculators short, and macro funds short. The author describes CESCO and LME sentiment as bearish without a stated reason.
The US-export arbitrage is viewed as controlled by one person. The author maintains that US downstream development relies on upstream metal availability.
Steel and aluminium are viewed as tariff winners. Rare earths and the US/China relationship are the main complexity.
The two charts the author relies on show how oversold copper miners are and what happens when a market prices a stockout.

Markets that got short a commodity and worried about a stockout rallied sharply: gas in 2022, cocoa in 2024, alumina in 2023, bauxite in 2025, lumber during covid, and steel (5x after covid). Alumina and bauxite were bearish outcomes, and neither was supply constrained as copper is.
The author says the GSXGCOPP basket pays if demand improves, supply disappoints, or tariffs come in, and all three are priced in the basket at an 8-month low.
The basket has had the tail of smaller COPX names removed, has balance sheet support of 0.0-0.5x net debt/EBITDA, a seasonality tailwind, and a P/B long/short ratio at a 6-month low.

For a single stock, the author says the market keeps coming back to Anglo American (AAL.LN). Reported remedy discussions are nearing conclusion with no structural remedies currently being discussed, per a third source (paywalled).
Anglo sequence the market is following: diamonds deal completion, nickel (EU ruling date Dec 21, c.$500m), Teck deal approval ('the main game'), then the coal deal.
After Teck deal close: dividend 45 days post close, and an index event with feedback of more than $5bn of passive demand.
The coal deal needs FIRB approval (1Q target), with $2.3bn upfront and $1.575bn over a 5-year earn-out. The author notes no buyback has been announced.
Glencore has bought about 58% of its $500m buyback, which the author cites as a read on how miners with buybacks view their stock at these levels.

market_movers.rationale: Anglo American (AAL.LN, no US listing): the market keeps returning to the stock. Remedy discussions on the Teck deal are reported to be nearing conclusion with no structural remedies discussed.
Glencore (GLEN.LN, no US listing): has bought about 58% of its $500m buyback, cited as how miners with buybacks are responding to lower prices.

sector_views.rationale: Copper miners are oversold, with the basket at an 8-month low, low leverage, a seasonality tailwind and a P/B long/short ratio at a 6-month low.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The author says a lot of risk premium has been removed. A tariff would send the price back up sharply.

trade_ideas.description: Buy GSXGCOPP March 130%/140% call spread (copper miners basket), cost 1% for a 10x pay-out
trade_ideas.rationale: The trade pays if demand improves, supply disappoints or tariffs come in, and the author says all three are priced in the basket, which is at an 8-month low.
trade_ideas.risk: Maximum loss is the premium paid (1%).

risk_factors: Without a tariff, copper may stay weak while positioning remains short.
A stockout being priced can be read as bullish or bearish. Alumina and bauxite were bearish outcomes.
Anglo American's deal sequence depends on remedy outcomes, the EU's Dec 21 nickel ruling date, Teck approval and FIRB approval for the coal deal.
vol_and_positioning: CTAs, China speculators and macro funds are all short copper.
The GSXGCOPP Mar 130%/140% call spread costs 1% of notional for a 10x pay-out, with maximum loss limited to the premium paid.
The GSXGCOPP basket is at an 8-month low, and the P/B long/short ratio is at a 6-month low.
geopolitical: US tariffs on copper are the main upside trigger cited.
Rare earths and the US/China relationship are cited as the main complexity.
Anglo American and Teck deal remedy discussions and approvals are ongoing.

tension_points.bull_case: Copper at $12.5k has had risk premium removed, CTAs, China speculators and macro are short, and a tariff, demand improvement or supply disappointment would trigger a sharp rally.
tension_points.bear_case: A stockout priced into a market has been bearish in some cases (alumina in 2023, bauxite 2025), and the morning note cites bearish sentiment at CESCO and LME.
tension_points.what_invalidates: No tariff arriving, with demand and supply not changing, leaves the call spread to expire worthless (max loss is the 1% premium).
